_note: Inputs to cost_model.py. Token counts and latencies here are the PRODUCTION estimates (real provider, real web sources) that the architecture is budgeted against. The offline spike is much cheaper and faster; `cost_model.py --calibrate <trace.jsonl>` prints the measured spike numbers next to these so the gap is visible rather than hidden. Rate card mirrors prototype/agent/models.py RATE_CARD.

stages.name: guardrail.input
stages.note: Cheap screen before any spend; a blocked run costs only this.

stages.name: worker.search
stages.note: Tool-only, no model call. Latency is search-API bound.

stages.name: worker.fetch
stages.note: Open-web fetch: the fattest latency tail in the system.

stages.name: worker.summarize
stages.note: Extractive summary per source. This is what keeps raw docs out of synthesis.

stages.name: orchestrator.synthesize
stages.note: Dominant cost driver: evidence tokens are paid on every synthesis attempt.

stages.name: guardrail.output
stages.note: Groundedness + PII screen over the finished report.

fanout._note: Worker stages run concurrently, so their contribution to wall-clock is the SLOWEST worker, not the sum. Cost, by contrast, scales linearly with width. `evidence_per_subquestion` is how many summaries per sub-question reach synthesis; capping it is lever L3.

retries._note: A retried worker re-pays for its own stage only; checkpointing means a process restart re-pays nothing already committed.

budget._note: Envelope is the defended constraint; the ceiling is enforced live in the orchestrator (budget_guard). Reserve covers eval-suite runs, re-baselining and incident replay.

latency_budget._note: User-facing budget for the read-only path. The HITL export path is explicitly out of budget: it waits on a human.
